gloss: thin round slicing; cutting into thin rounds

definitions.gloss: thin round slicing; cutting into thin rounds; cross-cutting into thin circles
definitions.explanation: A cooking technique of cutting cylindrical vegetables (like green onions, cucumbers, or carrots) crosswise into thin round slices. One of the basic Japanese cutting techniques.

examples.japanese: ネギを{小口切|こぐちぎ}りにする。
examples.english: To slice green onions into thin rounds.

examples.japanese: きゅうりを{小口切|こぐちぎ}りにして{塩|しお}をふる。
examples.english: Slice the cucumber into thin rounds and sprinkle with salt.

examples.japanese: {味噌汁|みそしる}の{仕上|しあ}げにネギの{小口切|こぐちぎ}りを{散|ち}らす。
examples.english: Scatter thinly sliced green onion rounds over the miso soup as a finishing touch.

notes:
A compound of {小口|こぐち} (small edge/end face) + {切|ぎ}り (cutting). Refers specifically to cutting from the end of a cylindrical vegetable, producing thin circular slices. A fundamental technique in Japanese cooking.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {小口切|こぐちぎ}りにする: to cut into thin rounds
- ネギの{小口切|こぐちぎ}り: thinly sliced green onion
- {薄|うす}い{小口切|こぐちぎ}り: thin round slices

OTHER JAPANESE CUTTING TECHNIQUES:
- {千切|せんぎ}り: julienne — cutting into thin matchstick strips
- {乱切|らんぎ}り: rolling cut — cutting at irregular angles for even cooking
- {輪切|わぎ}り: round slicing — similar to {小口切|こぐちぎ}り but thicker slices
- {斜|なな}め{切|ぎ}り: diagonal cut — slicing at an angle
- みじん{切|ぎ}り: mincing — cutting into very fine pieces
